subject: Announcement: insertUI and removeUI functions now available on Shiny's development version

messages.author: 3a0f8d061378e811
messages.subject: Announcement: insertUI and removeUI functions now available on Shiny's development version
parts:
Hi shiny folks,

I’m a recent addition to the Shiny team at RStudio and I wanted to let you all know that we’ve just added a pretty exciting new feature to Shiny’s development version (install it with: devtools::install_github("rstudio/shiny”)).

There’s two new functions: insertUI and removeUI, which allow you to add and remove arbitrary pieces of UI to your app. The best way to familiarize yourself with these might be to check out this demo app and read this article.

We’re guessing that a lot of you might find this feature useful, so we’d really appreciate if you could try it out and lets us know if you encounter any problems (or just general feedback). We’re hoping to release to CRAN in the coming weeks.


I’ll leave you with parts of the documentation and minimal examples:

insertUI

This function allows you to dynamically add an arbitrarily large UI object into your app, whenever you want, as many times as you want. Unlike renderUI, the UI generated with insertUI is not updatable as a whole: once it's created, it stays there. Each new call to insertUI creates more UI objects, in addition to the ones already there (all independent from one another). To update a part of the UI (ex: an input object), you must use the appropriate render function or a customized reactive function. To remove any part of your UI, use removeUI.

Note that whatever UI object you pass through ui, it is always wrapped in an extra div (or if inline = TRUE, a span) before making its way into the DOM. This does not affect what you mean to do, and it makes it easier to remove the whole UI object using removeUI (if you wish to do so, of course).


Example:

## Only run this example in interactive R sessions
if (interactive()) {
# Define UI
ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("add", "Add UI")
)

# Server logic
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$add, {
    insertUI(
      selector = "#add",
      where = "afterEnd",
      ui = textInput(paste0("txt", input$add),
                     "Insert some text")
    )
  })
}

# Complete app with UI and server components
shinyApp(ui, server)
}


removeUI

This function allows you to remove any part of your UI. Once removeUI is executed on some element, it is gone forever. While it may be a particularly useful pattern to pair this with insertUI (to remove some UI you had previously inserted), there is no restriction on what you can use removeUI on. Any element that can be selected through a jQuery selector can be removed through this function.


Example:

## Only run this example in interactive R sessions
if (interactive()) {
# Define UI
ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("rmv", "Remove UI"),
  textInput("txt", "This is no longer useful")
)

# Server logic
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$rmv, {
    removeUI(
      selector = "div:has(> #txt)"
    )
  })
}

# Complete app with UI and server components
shinyApp(ui, server)
}

parts:
I have two initial comments:
- I think it'd be useful for a lot of users to mention that if you want to add multiple UI elements, then you need to wrap them in a div or tagList. I can see many people trying to use the 'ui' argument as 'ui = textInput(), textInput()'
- I'm not sure if this one has an ideal solution, but when I use afterEnd I would expect new UI elements to show up after previous ones that were added. In the example you give in the above sample code, I expect every new elemtn to be added at the bottom of the page, not above the previously inserted elements. I understand why it happens, but I think it's not what people would intuitively expect or want.  But maybe it is the correct thing to do, not sure.

Very useful feature!

messages.author: 3a0f8d061378e811
messages.subject: Re: Announcement: insertUI and removeUI functions now available on Shiny's development version
parts:
Hi Dean,

Thanks for your feedback!

I think your first comment is a really good catch, I'll be sure to update the documentation to reflect that :)

As for the second suggestion, I definitely struggled with that. This is what the `where` argument was based off of. I totally understand your intuition and initially felt the same way. However, since `where` is always relative to the `selector`, I don't think there's a very elegant way to add elements after one another, instead of the more stack-like format that `afterEnd` produces. There is a workaround, however, which is to use `beforeEnd` instead -- `beforeEnd` makes newly inserted elements children of the `selector` element, so it's definitely a bad idea to use it is your `selector` is a button or something like that. But if your `selector` is a just a placeholder div, then, this produces the result you intended: `beforeEnd` always adds the new element as the *last* child of the `selector` element, so the visual result is that things get inserted one after another. This is actually why `beforeEnd` is the default. It is also the pattern I use for the demo app (use a placeholder as `selector` and stick to the `beforeEnd` default). Maybe I should make this clearer in the documentation or the article. Do you feel like this is enough flexibility for the user?

Thanks again, really helpful to get a pair of fresh eyes on this!
Barbara

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: Re: Announcement: insertUI and removeUI functions now available on Shiny's development version
parts:
Yes that's enough flexibility, and as I said I recognize it's something that might no really have an ideal solution. I just wanted to make sure this "issue" has been considered, and it looks like you did think about it.

Another thing that just popped into my mind: this feature sounds like it could work nicely with modules.  You can imagine having a few UI elements that are grouped together into a module and wanting to insert that module dynamically.  Has this idea been looked at as well? If it's easy to make them work together, that's awesome.  Though it might not be very easy to support that, I'm not sure.

One last comment: When removing inputs, the user needs to know how to write the exact (sometimes complex) javascript expression to capture the correct element. Have you considered doing something similar to what I do in shinyjs, where I try to automatically detect if the id corresponds to an input or not, which makes it a lot easier to use?  https://github.com/daattali/shinyjs/blob/master/inst/srcjs/shinyjs-default-funcs.js#L48-L57
It's a tadeoff between trying to be helpful and making too many (potentially dangerous?) assumptions.

ui <- fluidPage(
  shinyjs::useShinyjs(),
  uiOutput("selectPlaceholder"),
  actionButton("toggle", "toggle"), br(), br(),

actionButton("add", "Add UI")
)

# Server logic
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$add, {
    insertUI(
      selector = "#add",
      where = "afterEnd",
      ui = textInput(paste0("txt", input$add),

paste0("Insert some text ", input$add))
    )
  })
  
  output$selectPlaceholder <- renderUI({
    inputs <- grep("^txt\\d+$", names(input), value = TRUE)
    selectInput("select", "Select an input to toggle", choices = inputs)
  })
  
  observeEvent(input$toggle, {
    shinyjs::toggleState(input$select)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

On Thursday, May 5, 2016 at 9:11:49 AM UTC-5, bar...@rstudio.com wrote:
Hi shiny folks,

I’m a recent addition to the Shiny team at RStudio and I wanted to let you all know that we’ve just added a pretty exciting new feature to Shiny’s development version (install it with: devtools::install_github("rstudio/shiny”)).

There’s two new functions: insertUI and removeUI, which allow you to add and remove arbitrary pieces of UI to your app. The best way to familiarize yourself with these might be to check out this demo app and read this article.

We’re guessing that a lot of you might find this feature useful, so we’d really appreciate if you could try it out and lets us know if you encounter any problems (or just general feedback). We’re hoping to release to CRAN in the coming weeks.


I’ll leave you with parts of the documentation and minimal examples:

insertUI

This function allows you to dynamically add an arbitrarily large UI object into your app, whenever you want, as many times as you want. Unlike renderUI, the UI generated with insertUI is not updatable as a whole: once it's created, it stays there. Each new call to insertUI creates more UI objects, in addition to the ones already there (all independent from one another). To update a part of the UI (ex: an input object), you must use the appropriate render function or a customized reactive function. To remove any part of your UI, use removeUI.

Note that whatever UI object you pass through ui, it is always wrapped in an extra div (or if inline = TRUE, a span) before making its way into the DOM. This does not affect what you mean to do, and it makes it easier to remove the whole UI object using removeUI (if you wish to do so, of course).


Example:

## Only run this example in interactive R sessions
if (interactive()) {
# Define UI
ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("add", "Add UI")
)

# Server logic
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$add, {
    insertUI(
      selector = "#add",
      where = "afterEnd",
      ui = textInput(paste0("txt", input$add),
                     "Insert some text")
    )
  })
}

# Complete app with UI and server components
shinyApp(ui, server)
}


removeUI

This function allows you to remove any part of your UI. Once removeUI is executed on some element, it is gone forever. While it may be a particularly useful pattern to pair this with insertUI (to remove some UI you had previously inserted), there is no restriction on what you can use removeUI on. Any element that can be selected through a jQuery selector can be removed through this function.


Example:

## Only run this example in interactive R sessions
if (interactive()) {
# Define UI
ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("rmv", "Remove UI"),
  textInput("txt", "This is no longer useful")
)

# Server logic
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$rmv, {
    removeUI(
      selector = "div:has(> #txt)"
    )
  })
}

# Complete app with UI and server components
shinyApp(ui, server)
}
